newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends active session with modest gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends active session with modest gains.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended modestly firmer at C$1.3498 (US$0.7408) from Monday's close at C$1.3510 (US$0.7401), but softer from early morning levels around C$1.3468 (US$0.7425)
* Canada unit buffeted by U.S. dollar volatility against Asian, European currencies, traders said * Canadian currency seen trading between C$1.3485 and C$1.3520 overnight.

Profit takers took the U.S. dollar broadly lower on Tuesday. The U.S. currency briefly moved below the key 113 yen level earlier in the session, partly due to the yen's strength against the British pound.
The pound weakened sharply on Tuesday after British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said British business is worried about the sterling's strength.
In Canada, traders said they expect the Canadian dollar to trade between C$1.3485 and C$1.3520 overnight. "We may test the upside again overnight or early Wednesday morning," one trader said.
Economists have said the fundamentals for the unit were still positive.

Last week's solid third quarter gross domestic product numbers suggested stronger growth for the Canadian economy. But all eyes in the market will be on Canada's November employment report due out Friday.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar edged up to 1.1518 marks from 1.1508 on Monday, but slipped to 83.85 yen from 84.73 yen on Monday.
